newsitem.title: USA: Stimsonite plans cost cutting measures.
newsitem.headline: Stimsonite plans cost cutting measures.

text.p: Stimsonite Corp said Friday it will not relocate its its principal manufacturing and administrative functions to a new site in Chicago and plans other cost cutting measures including a 10 percent reduction in the company's workforce.

"After a careful process of reengineering the company, we concluded that the company is best served by continuing to lease its current facilities rather than invest approximately $14 million in a new facility," said Jay Taylor, president.
"We have extended our current building lease for 10 years at a favorable rate," he said in a statment.

Taylor said the company has realized some manufacturing process efficiencies recently which have decreased space requirements. He said the company could support expected volume growth over the next few years with its current facilities. He also noted that additional manufacturing and office space would likely be available in Niles within the next few years to satisfy longer term needs.
As previously announced, Stimsonite had begun construction of a 137,000 square foot manufacturing and office facility in the Chicago metropolitan area.
The company said it intends to sell the property and will begin marketing it within the next few weeks.

Stimsonite said it is taking other actions under a reengineering program designed to reduce expenses and improve efficiency. These actions include a personnel reduction of about 10 percent of the salaried workforce.

In connection with these actions, Stimsonite said it expects to record a supplemental one-time pre-tax charge of about $4 million to cover the potential loss upon disposition of the property, severance expenses and other costs related to the restructuring.
